brief: 6 investor red flags founders learn the hard way — avoid these at all costs.

slots.body: Six warning signs that separate toxic capital from true partners. Ignore them and pay the price later.

slots.title: They Pressure You To Sign
slots.body: Any investor demanding a signature within days is hiding something. Smart founders always involve counsel before committing.
slots.calloutBody: Never sign a term sheet without independent legal review, no matter how urgent the deadline feels.

slots.title: Founder References Are Missing
slots.body: If they will not connect you with portfolio founders, assume the relationship ends badly. Great investors open their network proudly.
slots.calloutBody: Cold-message two founders from their portfolio before you ever accept a meeting or term sheet.

slots.title: Dirty Terms Hide Inside Deals
slots.body: Non-standard pro-rata, excessive liquidation preferences, or random veto rights can cripple your company. Read every clause carefully.
slots.calloutBody: If the term sheet deviates from standard SAFE or Series A docs, demand a written explanation for every change.

slots.title: Money Is Their Only Weapon
slots.body: Capital without strategic introductions or operational support is expensive dead weight. The best investors actively help you hire and sell.
slots.calloutBody: Ask exactly how they helped their last three portfolio companies beyond wiring the funds.

slots.title: Terms Change After The Handshake
slots.body: Verbal agreements mean nothing if they alter economics during final docs. This behavior predicts every future boardroom battle.
slots.calloutBody: The moment terms shift post-handshake, end the conversation immediately and preserve your leverage elsewhere.

slots.title: Other Founders Quietly Warn You
slots.body: Whispers about micromanagement, blame-shifting, or legal threats are common in private forums. Believe patterns, not polished pitches.
slots.calloutBody: Search founder forums and anonymous lists for their name before you celebrate the term sheet.

slots.body: Fundraising is a filter, not just a chase. Vet investors with the same intensity they use to vet you.
